issue.description: Open-template reporting obligations appear in two canonical requirements: CAND-00081 (Query tool and open-template reporting) and CAND-00119 (Open Template Reporting). The overlap risks conflicting scope and permissions; consider consolidating into a single open-template requirement.
issue.suggested_fix: Choose one canonical open-template requirement and merge scope/permissions; remove one of the duplicates; ensure a single, traceable ID for open-template reporting.

reason: Open-template/reporting appears in multiple candidate statements (CAND-00081 and CAND-00119) with overlapping scope; the SRS must consolidate to a single canonical requirement to avoid inconsistent scope and permissions.

issue.description: Audit/deletion auditing appears in multiple candidates (e.g., CAND-00043 Audit Trail for Purges; CAND-00049 Database Trigger for Deletions; CAND-00050 Deletion Interface). The duplication could cause inconsistent audit data or gaps.
issue.suggested_fix: Consolidate into a single deletion/audit requirement with explicit audit fields and a single mechanism (e.g., DB trigger + report interface) and map all related items to that canonical requirement.

reason: Deletion/audit capabilities are expressed across several candidates (e.g., CAND-00043, CAND-00049, CAND-00050) — the specification needs a single, authoritative deletion-audit requirement (mechanism, fields and UI) to prevent gaps or conflicts.

issue.description: In-transit reporting appears in several candidates with similar scope (CAND-00033; CAND-00100; CAND-00150): per-branch/system, configurable X days, and merging transit-to/from. This duplication may cause conflicting behavior.
issue.suggested_fix: Consolidate to a single In-Transit Items Report definition and reference it from related requirements; ensure the default detection rule and fields are consistent.

reason: In-transit reporting requirements recur in multiple candidates (CAND-00033, CAND-00100, CAND-00150) with the same but separately-worded expectations (X days, merged transit-to/from); the spec should consolidate to one definitive in-transit report definition and detection rule set.

issue.description: Shelf-space reporting has a decided approach to estimation but the method is open to choices; CAND-00015 documents possible estimation methods but no fixed policy.
issue.suggested_fix: Decide and document a default shelf-space calculation method (e.g., use item-count proxies with documented estimation method) and mark alternatives as optional design options.

reason: Shelf-space estimation method is deliberately left as an implementation/choice question and the spec already permits calculated estimates and requires documenting the method used (CAND-00015); this open question is valid, not a defect to force a single algorithm.

issue.description: Historical reporting vs. real-time reporting architecture is unclear. The open-question references CAND-00121, CAND-00211, CAND-00215 about warehouse/snapshots vs real-time and retention; Decide and document an approach.
issue.suggested_fix: Select and document the historical reporting architecture, update to reflect either snapshot warehouse or real-time plus historical, and define data refresh and retention semantics; unify the historical reporting mode.

reason: Historical vs. real-time architecture is a documented design choice in the corpus (the SRS permits either replicas/warehouse or properly-written SQL and requires documenting the chosen approach), so leaving the architectural decision open is intentional and not a defect.

issue.description: Auto-revert precedence for item transfers is ambiguous; overlapping inputs CAND-00022 and CAND-00027 describe time-based and event-based reversion; define a clear precedence (e.g., time-based revert unless a qualifying event occurs).
issue.suggested_fix: Add explicit precedence rules to saved transfers; define event-trigger definitions and override behavior; ensure admin-configured overrides preserved.

reason: Precedence between time-based and event-based auto-revert is already addressed in the transfer-utility text (explicit precedence rules and documentation required); the specification already requires documenting how overrides interact, so this is not an unresolved defect.

issue.description: Capacity-related requirements are described across multiple candidates with overlapping scope/naming (e.g., High-Level Overview, Drill-down, Trends, color-coding, grouping). Risk of inconsistent scope and duplication.
issue.suggested_fix: Consolidate into a single capacity analytics/dashboard definition with a clear set of features and traceability to related options; keep separate options as design-time variants but map to one canonical ID.

reason: Capacity/dashboard concerns are already consolidated under the System capacity interface requirement (it aggregates drill-down, sorting, filters, color-coding and grouping); the corpus provides a single canonical requirement mapping the related candidate IDs, so no further defect to record here.

issue.description: Inactive-patrons reporting appears in many candidates with overlapping scope (CAND-00059, CAND-00061, CAND-00062, CAND-00063, CAND-00103, CAND-00236, CAND-00259, CAND-00060, CAND-00278, CAND-00279); unify to a single inactive-patrons reporting capability with consistent scope and auditing.
issue.suggested_fix: Consolidate into a single inactive-patrons reporting feature with uniform scope levels and a single export/audit workflow.

reason: Inactive-patrons reporting and outreach-export needs are consolidated in the dedicated Inactive patrons reporting requirement (covers configurable X, scopes, exports, exclusions and background processing); duplicates across candidates reflect provenance rather than a missing/contradictory requirement.
